notes.title: 10 years since release of Sylvio
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8831055/3fce94a523c613e9b272e2dc0b26d35ca6457537.png"][/img][/p][p]I was renting a small office desk in Stockholm at the time, me and five other people crammed together on 25 square meters on two floors. Nowadays I think it's a science fiction bookstore. Anyway, I was mostly alone in that office, the others had steady jobs, freelancing on the side. I'd been sitting there 6 days a week, 12 hours a day for two and a half years by now. I'd learnt Unity and built a game at the same time, and now I'd just pressed the green button on Steam. Almost immediately I got a message from someone, telling me he was unable to pick up the very first item, basically breaking the game after the first 30 seconds of playing. I buried my face and broke down in the tiny wooden stairs we had leading up to the second floor. So much work, so much pressure and built up impostor syndrome, I've never had that feeling of melting brain before. After a while I managed to pick up what was left of my head and check the game myself, and of course I was able to pick it up, and so were apparently some other people too, because I'd started to receive some reviews. 

It took me on some adventures this game, going to the TIGA awards, receiving reviews and articles, juggling a simultaneous port and release to XBOX One and PS4, and finally getting to create Sylvio: Black Waters with Dread XP. 

I'm not going to write long, what I really just wanted to say is thank you for playing, and thank you to you all for the encouragement and interest you've shown along the way. 

Stroboskop has a couple of different projects in the pipeline, and stuff will be revealed when the time is right. In the meantime, have a great day / night / whatever you're having. 

Much love and all the best,[/p][p]Niklas[/p]

notes.title: SYLVIO UPDATE
notes.notes:
[b]Important stuff first:[/b]

[list]
[*] Added the ability to Run.
[*] Added Custom Key Binding.
[*] Rearranged the gameplay in the second level, to make it more intuitive.
[*] Took away the combination lock function on all lockers. I've always seen it as a feature creep, and it makes the game unplayable for deaf players. 
[*] Killed some long-living bugs. 
[*] Various cosmetica.
[/list]

It's been five years since the last update. The release of Sylvio 2 caused me to burn out of gamedev I got back into working as a freelance composer, I co-founded an environmental startup, coded some apps. In 2021 I dipped my toe into gamedev again, with a project called Guidance.

In the beginning of 2022, I got invited to join the Dread X Collection 5, a horror game collection put together by Dread XP. I had roughly two months to put together a game with a playtime of 45 minutes. 
Man, it was so intense, to just go from scratch zero to finished project in that short amount of time, but it was an amazing experience.

You can get the collection here. The game I made is called KARAO.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1899810/Dread_X_Collection_5/]https://store.steampowered.com/app/1899810/Dread_X_Collection_5/[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8831055/3fab6bae03115027502c924953113bb0548049fe.png[/img]

The experience made me relearn what it is I love about creating horror games. I am currently exploring paths for future horror game projects, and will keep you posted when something materialises. Guidance is put on hold for the moment.

Digging up the old Sylvio project and getting into that spaghetti code has been cleansing, in a way. I'm so thankful for all the people that have been playing it through the years, and as it's still being picked up by new players, it feels good to give it an update.

As always, let me know of any bugs, either on the forum or on bugs@stroboskop.com

If you have any problem with the new build, you can use the password Play2017Sylvio to access the old build. 

See you soon,
Niklas, Stroboskop

notes.title: Guidance : A new survival horror game from the creator of Sylvio
notes.notes:
[h1][b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1797400]Guidance[/url] is a survival horror game about spirit possession.[/b][/h1]

Play as Velvet, a golden-ager in search of his lost wife. Talk to spirits through the possessed, tranquillize the angry ones, and try to ignore those blackouts you're having.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41429091/4f6242e0000cc9ab74bf1f10f345c113afbf7f23.gif[/img]

Velvet, a senior citizen and retired electrician, is on a guided bus tour far out in the wilderness with his wife Jo. Coming across an old abandoned village, the guide decides to go off the planned schedule and take the group for a short improvised exploration. 

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41429091/1df659766f571d8c8f9c04fcfe7dd299cac69500.gif[/img]

Velvet, who chose to stay behind for a nap, wakes up alone several hours later in the dark bus. Equipped only with a tranquilizer gun he enters the village, determined to find his wife. 

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41429091/8caff406c0d23f22d6d0146a8b4ed0898e97418e.gif[/img]

Velvet communicates with the spirits that have possessed the other people from the group. His one and only concern is finding his wife, and will take any steps necessary in order to make that happen. 

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41429091/59eab8ada7c49a56843c390653215669f160f04a.gif[/img]

He doesn't care about the well-being of the other ones from the group. If they're a threat to his mission, or if they  turn up to be useful in some way, Velvet will take actions accordingly.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41429091/af79955c3fb4e5dbf23c50fed9a923b0f77fbd04.gif[/img]

The zoom-out seen in the trailer is a part of gameplay. You are able to fully zoom in and out during the game, to spot areas of interest or to plan your next move. Zooming in will reveal details around you, but might put you in danger of surprise attacks.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/41429091/44fe3cb4d1381ff78270fd5a80a383e63745631e.gif[/img]

Explore a meticulously detailed, boarded-up, abandoned village, overtaken by wild grass and moths. The street lights are triggered with motion detectors. This is your only source of light, and can be a good way to spot the others, before they spot you.

[b]Wishlist now![/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1797400

notes.title: The 25 Best Horror Games On PC
notes.notes:
To compile a list of the 25 best horror games on PC is to look into the void for so long that the void not only starts to look back, but shakes you by the hand and takes you out for coffee. It is to fight with monsters until you become a monster and then go on a European railtrip with the other monsters, and really bond over cocktails in Saint-Tropez.

It is also a great way to explore the wide range of possible experiences within horror fiction. Here, there is something for everyone, even the squeamish and the easily-startled. Yes, there are jumpscares, but there are also slow-burn psychological dramas and tongue-in-cheek splatterfests. There are uncanny things and real terrors, but there are smiles and smirks among the shocks.

notes.title: Quietly creepy ghost-recording sequel Sylvio 2 is out
notes.notes:
Sylvio is one of my favourite recent horror games. I described it as an “anti-screamer” because it’ll unnerve you with a whisper rather than startling you with a jumpscare. Most of the creepiness comes from listening to recordings of ghosts, playing tracks at various speeds and/or reversing them to hear the voices in the static. It also had bits where you shot giant shadowy figures and blobs. The sequel [official site], which came out yesterday, ditches the shooting and adds video recordings alongside the audio tapes. I’ve had a quick look and listen.

notes.title: Sylvio 2 grabs a camera for more spooking in autumn
notes.notes: In an age when most horror games and movies are seen through the grainy lens of the protagonist’s camcorder, we were delighted by 2015’s Sylvio instead picking up a reel-to-reel sound recorder. Wandering around an abandoned park to record strange noises and reveal ghostly messages by manipulating the tapes was a novel treat. Now developers Stroboskop have announced Sylvio 2 [official site] and… yes, it will pick up a movie camera. That sounds potentially a shame but I do trust Stroboskop will do something interesting with this equipment too. Here, watch the announcement trailer: … [visit site to read more]

notes.title: A major update!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! 

I've been away from Steam the last months, as I've been buried with porting Sylvio to PS4 and XBox One. Apologies for not hanging out in the forums as much as I use to. I've been answering e-mails though, and that's really the best way to get in contact. 
niklas@stroboskop.com if you want to say hi or bugs@sylviogame.com if you're having troubles.

Sylvio is being released on PS4 and XBox One Friday 13th, January 2017. During the porting I added some features like revisiting areas, nicer hand animations and a bunch of other stuff, and this update adds all of that to the PC and Mac version.

There’s been a lot of work done on optimizing the levels, and things should just run smoother over-all.

I have deleted two achievements, Photo Of The Face and Blood Of The Mist, because they didn’t make sense with the new ’revisit area’-function. 

That’s all for now, take care and if you run into any bugs, I’m very grateful if you let me know at bugs@sylviogame.com

Best,
Niklas

notes.title: New patch - Disappearing Orbs
notes.notes:
I've been fighting for a while with a bug where the black orbs from time to time becomes invisible. I've been in contact with the 3rd party developers who made the plugin I'm using, but no solution has yet been found.

At first I thought it was an obscure problem only appearing on macs - but it seems like a few players are experiencing it all the time on all platforms - which makes the issue a lot more alarming.

I've now scrapped the 3rd party plugin and built a variation of the orb natively in Unity. Hopefully this will eliminate any problems. The patch is now live.

Thank you!

//Niklas

notes.title: 2015 s Best Horror Game Returns: Sylvio Remastered
notes.notes:
I love Sylvio [official site]. It’s a psychological horror game about exploring a sprawling abandoned park, searching for EVP recordings, and it scared me so much that I couldn’t play it at night with my headphones on. Manipulating audio files – here presented as tapes that you can play backwards and forwards at various speeds – focuses your attention on every scratch and pop. You’re effectively staring into the static, waiting for recognisable words to emerge. And when they do, they bring warnings, threats and tragedies.

We already knew a sequel was in the works but now news reaches us of a remastered version of the original game. That’ll be out May 2nd.

… [visit site to read more]

notes.title: Good and bad and good news.
notes.notes:
Good news: The Greenlight campaign for Sylvio 2 sailed into the green in only 13 days. That means Sylvio 2 will without a doubt be released on Steam once it's finished. 

Bad news: The Kickstarter didn't go as well. It had more than 350 backers but unfortunately ended about 35% from the goal. Which means the developing of Sylvio 2 will be put on hold for the time being. The plan is to continue late 2016.

Good news: The original Sylvio will be remastered, adding full support for all types of controllers, new GUI, updated graphics and improved gameplay. This will be delivered in a free update later on this spring. 

For those of you who are interested in supporting the studio and following the progress, I've set up a page at Patreon. 2 $ a month will get you Sylvio 1 and 2 as a digital download, so it's worth checking out!

You can read more about it here: https://www.patreon.com/stroboskop

Thanks for now and I'll see you around! 
//Niklas

notes.title: Multimedia Nightmares: Sylvio 2 Kickstarter
notes.notes:
Sylvio [official site] is my favourite horror game of 2015. The story of a young ghost-hunter who travels through an abandoned park collecting EVP recordings, it’s creepy, unusual, and entirely devoid of jumpscares and gore. Sylvio relies on great audio design and a weirdly vague and unnerving story to make a home under your skin. It deserved to be a word of mouth success in the way that films like The Babadook and It Follows have been over in cinema-land. One of the diamonds in a rough genre.

Whatever the final numbers were, I’m glad that it has been enough of a success that a sequel is being planned. It’s live on Kickstarter now.

notes.title: Sylvio 2 is announced!
notes.notes:
It’s been an overwhelming and awesome first six months of the game. Sylvio has been labeled "the best horror game of the year", and is nominated for "Best Original Game" on the upcoming TIGA awards, alongside games like Dying Light, BloodBorne and Everybody's Gone To The Rapture. It's had tons of super reviews and play-throughs, and to all of you who mailed me with feedback and suggestions, thank you all for being such AAA+++ human beings. I'm more determined than ever to continue in trying to bring something original to the table of horror gaming, so without much further ado, let me tell you a little bit about the sequel to Sylvio.

Sylvio 2 is set in broad daylight through-out the game, in the days following a ravaging forest fire in Saginaw Family Park. Juliette Waters is once again the protagonist, and portrayed, just like last time, by the brilliant actress Maia Hansson Bergqvist. And she’s got a hold of some brand new equipment.

”Stelotron L-500”, the reel recorder from the original Sylvio, has been replaced with the ”Stelotron L-1000”. A  360° video camera and a portable TV, making it possible to record ghosts in both vision and audio. You can zoom in and scan your recordings for any ghosts caught on tape, and just as before, your recordings are playable forward / backward in normal speed, fast forward or slow motion.

And the thing is, you’ll be able to test all of this out real soon.

A playable pre-alpha demo will be released at December 1st, along with the Kickstarter Campaign, Steam Greenlight and the first game trailer.

That's it for now, we'll be in touch very soon. Follow twitter.com/stroboskops  for more screenshots and gifs from Sylvio 2, and don’t forget to check out and sign up for the mailing list at sylvio2.com . Happy Halloween!

Niklas Swanberg, Stroboskop

notes.title: GhostBuskers: Audio Horror Game Sylvio Has a Demo
notes.notes:
Sylvio [official site] is my favourite horror game of 2015. It’s a quiet game, set in an abandoned park where the sky runs red, and you’ll spend the majority of the playing time straining to hear voices in the static. Sylvio, you see, is a game about electric voice phenomena and its central scares are based around a tape deck, on which recordings made in the field can be played at various speeds, reversed and analysed. I’ve raved about the game at length and now there’s a demo available for you to try.

notes.title: New SAVE system added!
notes.notes:
After installing the latest patch, Sylvio saves your progress continuously during gameplay. This has been a feature that has been asked for since the launch, and I'm happy to announce it's now in place. 

Saving is done automatically and frequently, and stores all notes, collectibles, inventory and environment progress.

As always, please send me a mail at bugs@sylviogame.com if you experience any kind of weird glitch or bug.

//Niklas

notes.title: Invert Y-axis, smoothness on / off, right hand key mapping
notes.notes:
It's been a busy first week since the launch! A couple of requests from players has comed up, and in the latest update I've been able to cater some of them. You are now able to:

* Invert Y-axis 
* Turn camera smoothness on / off
* Play with right hand key mapping

The added keys are:

E (action) = Num 0
Q (cancel) = Delete
C (flashlight) = Page down
1-9 (mic, gun, inventory, reel recorder, sheet 1-5) = Num 1-9
Space (jump) = Shift

If you find any bugs, or whatever strange thing that might occur, please send a mail to bugs@sylviogame.com . I am very curious about your problems, and eager to eliminate them in the following updates. We'll keep in touch and  thanks for playing!

Niklas Swanberg

notes.title: Wot I Think: Sylvio
notes.notes:
Horror fans are poorly served and many, myself included, are gluttons for punishment. I try so many Slender-likes hoping to find a creepy idea or one good scare. It’s the same in film as in games I soak up exorcisms and found footage hoping to be spooked or unnerved, and usually walk away disappointed or disgusted.

It makes me very happy to say that recently released indie ghost hunting scare ‘em up Sylvio [official site] is an imaginative, unusual and frightening new horror game. Here’s wot I think.
